suma-international.title: Travel Services Website Design | Suma International

about.headline: When Intent Meets Uncertainty
about.body: People are ready to plan their journey, but hesitation wins before they reach out. Not due to lack of interest, but due to a lack of clarity, structure and trust in the service itself.

items.title: Too Many Variations
items.body: Packages come in many types and versions. Without a clear way to tell them apart, users struggle to find the one that fits them.

items.title: Trust Is Low
items.body: Travel involves money and commitment. Without visible proof of credibility, users default to caution and avoid making an inquiry.

items.title: Scattered Information
items.body: Details are spread across different places, making it hard for users to understand what they are asking for.

items.title: Outdated Design
items.body: A dated look weakens first impressions and makes the service feel less reliable before users read a single word.

items.title: No Visual Hierarchy
items.body: When everything looks equally important, users cannot tell where to look or what to do next.

items.title: Result
items.body: A gap forms between intent and action, where interested users leave before they inquire.

more.headline: Discovery Before Designing
more.body: The design started with understanding the business, not with screens. The project brief, the brand book and the eight service lines shaped the first decisions.

items.title: Options exist
items.body: but they are hard to compare

items.title: Information is available
items.body: but it is not in one place

items.title: The service is real
items.body: but it does not look trusted

more.closing: The challenge was not only usability. It was making a service feel clear and credible at every step.

suma-international.clientVoice: Our vision was to build a modern, professional website that presents all our travel services in one place. Customers should be able to explore Hajj & Umrah, visa assistance, hotel accommodation, holiday packages, customized tours, medical tourism and corporate travel, read our travel guides, and send an inquiry easily. The website needed to work well on desktop, tablet and mobile, load fast, and be built to perform in search. We also wanted a clear, trustworthy digital presence that reflects the quality of our company.
suma-international.solution:
This was never just about a good-looking travel website. It was about making people feel safe enough to ask. The design aims to reduce hesitation by giving users clear information and visible signals of trust.

01. Show Trust Early — Trust badges are part of the interface, so users can see credibility signals before they decide to inquire.

02. Describe Everything Clearly — Every service and package comes with a clear description. Users do not need to guess what is included or what they are asking for.

03. Make Packages Easy to Find — Services are organized so users can move from browsing to the right package with less effort.

04. Keep Services Transparent — Details are presented openly and in one place, so users can judge a service on facts, not assumptions.

extraSections.title: Information That Knows Its Place
extraSections.intro: The site is organized around what users need to know, in the order they need it. Each section introduces information at the moment it becomes relevant.

groups.title: Home Page
items: Company Overview: introduces who Suma is and what it does.
Featured Services: points users to the service that fits them.
Call to Action: gives users a clear next step.
Testimonials and Highlights: adds proof from others.

groups.title: Hero
items: Shows the package name and the main action.

groups.title: Overview
items: Gives a clear summary of the package.

groups.title: Itinerary
items: Lays out the trip step by step.

groups.title: Inquiry
items: Lets users ask without leaving the page.

extraSections.title: Service Transparency
paragraphs: In a high-trust decision, users look for clear answers, not promises. Services are described in plain language, and the information users need is easy to see. Nothing important is left for the user to find out later.

extraSections.title: Clear Packages, Easy Discovery
paragraphs: Packages are designed to be scanned, compared and found. Clear descriptions and a consistent structure help users understand each option and move toward the right one.

extraSections.title: Design That Carries Meaning
extraSections.headline: Visual design is not used to impress. It is used to guide attention, build credibility and make information easy to read.
paragraphs: Poppins (Font Family) — Typography That Reduces Effort. A clean type system with five weights, from Light to Bold, gives the content a clear hierarchy. Users can scan quickly and see what matters first.
Color That Signals Confidence. Teal leads actions and Deep Teal anchors headings. Gold appears only as a small accent. Colors follow a 60-30-10 balance.
Structure That Guides Attention. A 4pt spacing grid, 16px card radius and 8px button radius keep the layout consistent. Five elevation levels separate layers of content.
extraSections.closing: Desktop View: 1920px · Container: 1740px

extraSections.title: Designing for Real Impact
extraSections.intro: Impact is not always captured in numbers. It shows up in behavior. The design focuses on the moments where people usually pause, doubt or leave.

groups.title: Less Friction, More Forward Movement
items: A clear hierarchy guides users from discovery to inquiry with fewer decisions along the way.

groups.title: Visibility That Replaces Doubt
items: Clear descriptions and open information let users judge a service without relying on assumptions.

groups.title: Confidence Built Over Time
items: Trust signals appear across the journey, so confidence builds gradually instead of being asked for all at once.

testimonial.quote: Working with the Web Karigor team on our website was a great experience. They took our requirements and turned them into a clear, structured and professional design. The final result presents our services, packages and inquiry process in a modern, easy-to-navigate way, and reflects the quality of our company. We are happy with the approved design and appreciate the effort the Web Karigor team put into it.

kids-ecommerce.clientVoice: Shishu Poribohon aims to build a trusted e-commerce platform for children’s products, serving parents across Bangladesh and international customers through DHL-supported delivery. kids-ecommerce.solution: Shishu Poribohon addresses these challenges by creating a trust-focused shopping experience. times-today.title: Digital News Platform Design & Development | Times Today BD

about.headline: Building a Modern News Experience for a Connected Audience
about.body:
Times Today BD is a digital news platform designed to make news discovery and reading more structured, accessible, and engaging. Web Karigor focused on transforming an existing text-heavy experience into a clearer and more visually organized news platform.

The redesign addressed content hierarchy, navigation, readability, mobile usability, content discovery, and engagement. Every design decision focused on helping readers understand what matters, find relevant stories faster, and move naturally from one piece of content to the next.

more.headline: Designing Clarity Into the News Experience
more.body:
A news platform needs to communicate importance without overwhelming the reader. We improved the experience through stronger visual hierarchy, structured content presentation, clearer navigation, and responsive layouts.

The result is a more organized environment where breaking stories, important news, trending content, and individual articles can be understood and explored with less friction.

times-today.clientVoice: Times Today aims to deliver news from all over the world through a modern digital news platform. The goal was to create a more accessible and engaging experience where readers can discover important stories, navigate content easily, and read news comfortably across devices.
times-today.problem:
The existing Times Today experience lacked the structure and visual clarity expected from a modern digital news platform. Weak visual hierarchy, an underdeveloped homepage structure, difficult navigation, inconsistent UI, and a weaker mobile experience made it harder for readers to discover and consume content efficiently.

The article-reading experience and content discovery also required improvement, while limited engagement capabilities and weak advertisement integration reduced the overall effectiveness of the platform.
times-today.solution:
Web Karigor redesigned Times Today around a clearer editorial structure and a more readable digital experience. The solution focused on strengthening homepage hierarchy, improving article readability, simplifying navigation, supporting mobile news consumption, and creating stronger pathways for discovering related and trending content.

The platform was also supported by a structured design system and reusable components to maintain consistency across the experience. Development and UI implementation were completed by the Web Karigor team using Next.js and Laravel, followed by implementation review, design revisions, and UI QA.

testimonial.quote: The Times Today project was a great experience for our team. Web Karigor understood our vision and transformed it into a modern, responsive news platform with a much clearer structure and reading experience. The attention to detail, communication throughout the project, and ability to refine the product based on our requirements made the entire process smooth. We are pleased with the final platform and appreciate the team’s dedication from design through development and launch.
testimonial.name: Alexis Botaya

extraSections.title: Thinking Process
extraSections.intro: From research to launch, the project followed a structured design and development process focused on understanding the existing product, identifying usability gaps, and turning those findings into a clearer news experience.

phases.title: Discover
phases.intro: Understanding the product, audience, and content experience

items.title: Stakeholder Research
items.body: Understand business direction, content priorities, product requirements, and stakeholder expectations.

items.title: User Research

items.title: Competitive Analysis

items.title: Product & UX Audit
items.body: Evaluate the existing experience across hierarchy, navigation, readability, mobile usability, content discovery, engagement, and interface consistency.

items.title: Content Analysis
items.body: Understand how different types of news content need to be organized and presented for faster scanning and reading.

items.title: Information Structure

items.title: UI Design

items.body: Review the implemented interface against the approved design and identify visual or interaction differences.

items.body: Complete final revisions and checks before the platform went live.

extraSections.title: Information Architecture
extraSections.intro: The information architecture was designed around the way readers naturally consume news: discovering important stories, exploring categories, opening an article, continuing through related content, and returning to current or trending stories.
extraSections.closing: The structure was designed to reduce unnecessary friction between discovery and reading while giving readers multiple ways to continue exploring relevant content.

groups.title: Engagement Features
groups.intro: Helping readers interact with and continue exploring content

extraSections.title: Homepage Content Hierarchy
extraSections.headline: Turning a Content-Heavy Homepage Into a Clear Editorial Experience
paragraphs: A news homepage contains many competing pieces of information. Without clear hierarchy, breaking stories, important headlines, trending content, and secondary news can appear equally significant.
We redesigned the homepage around stronger visual prioritization so readers can quickly identify what matters most before exploring deeper into the platform.

The interface uses content positioning, scale, spacing, imagery, typography, and grouping to establish a clearer reading order. Instead of presenting news as a collection of equally weighted blocks, the homepage guides readers from the most important stories toward broader content discovery.
extraSections.closing: The result is a homepage that communicates editorial importance more clearly while giving readers a more natural path into the rest of the platform.

extraSections.title: Article Reading Experience
extraSections.headline: Making News Easier to Read and Understand
paragraphs: The article page is where the platform ultimately delivers its core value. A strong headline alone is not enough; the surrounding interface needs to support comfortable reading, clear context, and continued discovery.
We focused on improving the article experience through stronger typography, spacing, content structure, visual hierarchy, and related-content pathways.
The design gives the article itself the necessary focus while keeping supporting actions and discovery elements accessible without creating unnecessary distraction.
extraSections.closing: The result is a more focused reading environment that helps users consume an individual story while naturally connecting them to the wider news experience.

extraSections.title: Mobile News Experience
extraSections.headline: Designing News for Everyday Mobile Consumption
paragraphs: News consumption increasingly happens on smaller screens, where limited space makes hierarchy and readability even more important.

The Times Today experience was designed responsively rather than simply shrinking the desktop interface. Content blocks, navigation, typography, spacing, and interaction patterns were adapted to maintain clarity across different screen sizes.
The mobile experience prioritizes quick scanning while preserving the readability needed for longer article consumption.
extraSections.closing: The result is a more adaptable experience that keeps the core news journey clear across desktop and mobile environments.

extraSections.title: Trending News
extraSections.headline: Creating a Clear Path to What People Are Reading
paragraphs: Trending content provides another way for readers to discover stories beyond the primary editorial hierarchy.
We introduced a structured presentation for trending news so users can quickly identify content receiving attention and move from one story to another.
Rather than treating trending content as an isolated section, it works as part of the broader discovery experience, connecting readers with additional stories after their initial visit.
extraSections.closing: This creates an additional discovery layer that helps readers continue exploring the platform beyond the first story they encounter.

extraSections.title: News Engagement
extraSections.headline: Moving Beyond Passive Reading
paragraphs: A modern news platform needs to support more than simply opening and reading an article. Readers should have clear ways to interact with content and continue their journey through the platform.
Times Today was designed with engagement and continued discovery in mind, including content sharing, related news, trending stories, and notifications.
The experience connects these actions to the broader reading journey instead of treating engagement as separate functionality.
extraSections.closing: The goal was to create a more connected news experience where one article naturally leads to the next relevant piece of content.

extraSections.title: Design System
extraSections.headline: Building Consistency Across the News Platform
paragraphs: To maintain consistency across a content-heavy interface, Web Karigor established a reusable design system covering the primary visual and interactive elements of the platform.

The system includes typography, color, buttons, inputs, cards, navigation, tabs, badges, tags, news cards, article components, icons, image rules, interaction states, responsive components, and other reusable UI patterns.
extraSections.closing: The system was designed to maintain a consistent visual language while allowing different types of news content and interface states to remain distinguishable. Reusable components also helped keep the experience consistent during development and subsequent design revisions.

extraSections.title: Development & Launch
extraSections.headline: From Design to a Live News Platform
paragraphs: Following the design phase, the finalized interface was handed over to the Web Karigor development team for implementation.

The platform was developed using Next.js and Laravel, with the development team working closely with the approved Figma designs. Throughout implementation, Web Karigor maintained an iterative process where design and development were reviewed together.
Design revisions were made where required, followed by UI QA to ensure the implemented experience remained aligned with the intended interface.
The completed platform was then launched as a fully live responsive news website.

extraSections.title: Post-Launch
extraSections.headline: Continuing the Product Beyond Launch
paragraphs: The work continued after launch through ongoing product and technical improvements.
The post-launch process included bug fixes, developer support, content-related improvements, performance improvements, analytics-based iteration, and stakeholder-requested changes.
This allowed the platform to continue evolving beyond its initial launch while maintaining the foundation established during the design and development process.

extraSections.title: Results
extraSections.headline: A More Structured Digital News Experience
paragraphs: The redesigned Times Today platform is now live with a stronger visual structure, clearer content hierarchy, responsive layouts, and a more organized reading and discovery experience.
Following launch, the platform has reached approximately 200K monthly visitors and 500K+ monthly page views, with an average session duration of around 5 minutes or more.

The platform continues to receive mobile users, social engagement, and ongoing content activity, supported by continued performance improvements, analytics-based iteration, and stakeholder-driven updates.
The outcome is a more structured digital environment for delivering news, helping readers discover important stories, read comfortably across devices, and continue exploring relevant content.

kapital-properties.title: A Trusted Digital Experience for Modern Property Management | Kapital Properties Limited
titleLines: A Trusted Digital Experience for Modern Property Management

about.headline: Make property decisions feel clearer, more transparent and more connected.
about.body:
Kapital Properties came to Web Karigor with a vision that extended far beyond a conventional real-estate marketplace.

The goal was to create a technology-enabled ecosystem where people could discover, buy, sell, rent, finance and manage properties while accessing the professional services required throughout the property journey.

Our team translated that broad vision into a structured digital product experience. The resulting product brings property discovery, verification, financing, communication, property services and ongoing management into a single ecosystem.

more.headline: Designing for a Multi-Sided Property Experience
more.body:
The platform needed to work for people with very different intentions. A buyer may arrive with a budget and a location in mind. A seller may want to publish a property. A tenant may be looking for a suitable rental. An investor may be evaluating an opportunity. An NRB user may need someone in Bangladesh to inspect and manage a property on their behalf.

The client brief identifies property buyers, sellers, investors, landlords and tenants as core audiences, alongside institutional and professional stakeholders. Rather than forcing these users through the same experience, our team structured the product around their individual goals. The interface could then remain simple at the point of entry while progressively exposing the information and actions relevant to each journey.

kapital-properties.clientVoice:
Kapital Properties wanted to build a new kind of property service platform for Bangladesh: one that combines technology with professional human support rather than functioning only as a listing marketplace.

The vision covered the complete property journey, from finding or listing a property to financing, documentation, regulatory support, interiors and after-sale management. It was also designed to serve buyers, sellers, investors, landlords, tenants, businesses and Bangladeshis living abroad.

At the heart of the brief was a simple ambition: make property ownership and management more transparent, accessible and technology-enabled. Kapital Properties positioned this vision around trust, professionalism and human care.
kapital-properties.problem:
Real estate is rarely a single transaction. A person looking for a home may need to compare properties, understand ownership information, evaluate financing, communicate with a seller, arrange documentation and eventually manage the property.

For an owner, the journey can be completely different: listing a property, finding suitable buyers or tenants, handling documents, arranging inspections, managing rent and maintenance, and accessing professional services.

Kapital Properties wanted to bring these fragmented activities into one connected ecosystem. The challenge for Web Karigor was therefore not simply to design a property website. We had to translate a broad real-estate business model into a digital product that could accommodate different users, different journeys and different levels of service.
kapital-properties.solution:
We structured the product around discovery, evaluation, verification, financing, communication and ongoing management instead of treating property as a one-time listing transaction.

The work resulted in a digital product foundation covering property discovery, structured listing, trust and verification, a customer dashboard, financing, communication, property services, an NRB service model, investment-ecosystem concepts, Propertypulse News Network, and a shared design system.

For customers, the experience can move from finding a property to understanding it, verifying it, financing it, requesting support, and eventually managing the property.

testimonial.quote:
Working with Web Karigor gave us a clear direction for turning our vision for Kapital Properties into a complete digital property ecosystem. The team understood that we needed more than a property listing platform and translated our requirements into a structured, modern and user-focused experience covering property discovery, financing, services and management.

We appreciated the team’s ability to understand the complexity of our business and turn it into a product that feels clear, professional and trustworthy. Their attention to detail, communication and commitment throughout the project made the collaboration a valuable experience for Kapital Properties.
testimonial.name: Alexis Botaya

extraSections.title: Structuring the Property Experience
extraSections.intro: The property experience was organized as a clear path from first discovery to informed evaluation.

phases.title: Discover
phases.intro: The homepage concept centers around the message: Find. Finance. Own. Property discovery is supported by search, category navigation, filters and map-based exploration.

items.title: Buy · Rent · Commercial · New Projects
items.body: The original product brief specifically called for map view, filtering and category-based property exploration.

phases.title: Explore
phases.intro: A property card needs to communicate enough information to help someone decide whether to investigate further. Instead of treating the listing as a simple image-and-price card, the product architecture considers richer listing information.

items.title: Listing signals
items.body: Location, price, property type, key specifications, amenities, verification and media.

items.title: Deeper property data
items.body: The wider property data model also accounts for floor plans, ownership documents, mutation information, tax receipts and geolocation. The intention was to make important information discoverable before users commit to a deeper inquiry.

phases.title: Property Details
phases.intro: The property detail experience is where discovery turns into evaluation. The interface brings together the information a user needs to understand the property, its condition, location and legitimacy.

items.title: Information hierarchy
items.body: Property identity → Visual overview → Price & location → Key facts → Amenities → Detailed information → Documents → Location → Inquiry.

items.title: Verified media
items.body: The original brief also describes verified documents, photographs and 3D tours as part of the intended property experience. This approach gives users a clearer path from curiosity to informed consideration.

extraSections.title: Trust Is a Product Feature
paragraphs: For Kapital Properties, trust could not be treated as a branding exercise alone. The client defined a verification process involving NID, ownership papers, mutation records, bank verification and physical inspection before a property is published.

We reflected this requirement in the product experience by treating verification as visible product information rather than something hidden behind the scenes. The broader platform concept also includes verified profiles and a multi-layer fraud-prevention process combining automated moderation with manual review.
extraSections.closing: The design language therefore consistently favors clarity over ambiguity, evidence over assumption, and status over uncertainty.

extraSections.title: Listing a Property
extraSections.intro: Selling property requires a very different interaction model from discovering one. We structured the listing experience into clear stages so that a complex property submission could be completed progressively rather than through one overwhelming form.

groups.title: Listing Structure
items: 01 — Category: Choose the appropriate property category.
02 — Basic Information: Establish the property's fundamental identity.
03 — Location: Define where the property is located and provide relevant location information.
04 — Property Details: Capture specifications and characteristics.
05 — Amenities: Describe facilities and available features.
07 — Media Upload: Add property imagery and supporting visual material.

extraSections.closing: The wider platform also needs supporting documents such as title deeds, khatian, mutation records and tax receipts. The structure was designed to make the process understandable to ordinary property owners while giving KPL the information required for verification.

extraSections.title: Beyond Buying and Selling
extraSections.intro: One of the defining characteristics of the product is that property does not disappear from the platform after a transaction. Kapital Properties also offers a broader set of services.

groups.title: Service ecosystem
items: Property Selling — Technology-supported property marketing and sales assistance.
Property Buying — Verified property discovery with professional guidance.
Property Renting — Connecting tenants and landlords while simplifying documentation and management.
Property Financing — Loan eligibility, EMI calculation and application assistance.
Documentation & Logistics — Support for agreements, transfers, mutation, registration and tax documentation.
Regulatory Services — Assistance with approvals, VAT, tax and registration.
Interior Solutions — Interior services from concept through completion.
Property Management — Rent collection, maintenance, tenant management, inspection, valuation and compliance.

extraSections.closing: These services are part of the client's documented vision for an end-to-end property platform.

extraSections.title: Finance Within the Property Journey
extraSections.headline: Check Your Eligibility in 60 Seconds
paragraphs: Financing was not treated as an unrelated financial tool. It was designed as part of the property decision itself.
The intended experience connects: Property → Financing requirement → Eligibility → EMI → Application → Status.

The platform brief calls for loan eligibility checking, EMI calculation and direct application submission to partner banks. The homepage concept therefore gives financing a prominent position through an eligibility experience rather than burying it inside a secondary service page.
Specific banking integrations were identified in the client brief as being under process, so we have not represented them as confirmed production integrations.

extraSections.title: The User Dashboard
paragraphs: A property ecosystem needs somewhere for the customer's ongoing activities to live. The dashboard brings together the user's relationship with Kapital Properties instead of forcing them to repeatedly return to individual pages.

The documented platform requirements include tracking listings, favorites, chat history and loan applications. The broader UX structure extends this thinking into property requests, bookings, services and account activity.
extraSections.closing: The dashboard therefore acts less like a generic account page and more like a personal property workspace.

extraSections.title: Requests, Bookings & Human Assistance
paragraphs: Real estate does not always follow a fully automated transaction model. For KPL, certain actions require review, communication and professional involvement.

We therefore designed request and booking interactions around a clear processing model rather than pretending every transaction could happen instantly. A user can initiate an action, after which the request can move through an administrative process.

This reflects the client's stated payment model: initial booking fees and service payments may be handled online, while full property payments and transfers are handled offline with legal documentation.
extraSections.closing: The result is a product that acknowledges how real property transactions actually work instead of forcing them into a conventional e-commerce checkout model.

extraSections.title: Communication
paragraphs: Communication is another layer connecting the marketplace with KPL's professional service model. The intended platform includes secure chat, calls and inquiry so buyers and sellers can communicate without directly exposing personal contact information.
The product also supports communication around requests and services, creating a continuous relationship between the customer and KPL rather than ending the experience at the property detail page.

extraSections.title: A Dedicated Experience for NRBs
paragraphs: Non-Resident Bangladeshis represent a particularly different property journey. Someone living abroad may want to purchase, inspect, invest in, rent or manage property in Bangladesh without being physically present for every step.
Kapital Properties explicitly identifies NRBs as an important audience and positions its platform as a bridge between Bangladesh-based property services and people living abroad.
extraSections.closing: This makes the NRB experience fundamentally service-led rather than simply another property-search interface.

extraSections.title: Extending the Ecosystem Through Amana
extraSections.intro: The wider product vision also explored an ecosystem of specialized property and financial services under the Amana concept.

groups.title: Amana concepts
items: Amanafi — Islamic property and home-finance oriented services.
Amana Assets — Property-share and asset-oriented investment experiences.
Amana Crowd — A Shariah-aligned property crowdfunding concept.
Amana Agents — An agent and referral-oriented service layer.

extraSections.closing: These concepts were considered as extensions of the broader property ecosystem rather than replacements for the core marketplace. Because the supplied KPL brief does not provide detailed implementation specifications for these services, we treat them as part of the broader product work rather than claiming specific production functionality beyond what was established.

extraSections.title: Property Management Doesn't End at the Transaction
extraSections.headline: Discover. Acquire. Manage. Maintain. Grow.
paragraphs: Kapital Properties wanted to remain useful after a property is bought, sold or rented. The property management offering covers areas such as rent collection, maintenance, tenant management, inspections, valuation and compliance.

That changes the product relationship from a one-time transaction into a longer property lifecycle. The UX architecture reflects that longer relationship by keeping property information, requests, communication and services connected to the user's account.

extraSections.title: Propertypulse News Network
paragraphs: The product also includes a knowledge layer through Propertypulse News Network (PNN). Rather than treating content as a conventional company blog, the concept positions PNN around market trends, expert commentary, property analytics, regulatory changes, buyer guides and behavioral trends.

The client describes PNN as a source of data-driven property insights designed to help buyers, sellers and investors make more informed decisions. The homepage concept therefore includes a dedicated PNN section alongside the marketplace and financial tools.

extraSections.title: Designing for Bangladesh
paragraphs: The product was conceived as a bilingual experience supporting Bangla + English across listings, content, notifications and blogs.

This requirement influenced the product architecture beyond simply adding a language switch. Content-heavy property interfaces need to remain readable in both languages, while forms, notifications and service information need to preserve their hierarchy regardless of language.
extraSections.closing: The design direction therefore favors clear typography, generous spacing and structured content rather than overly dense interfaces.

extraSections.title: The Design System
extraSections.headline: Trustworthy. Modern. Professional. Human.
paragraphs: The visual system was created around the personality Kapital Properties wanted to establish. The client's original direction specified a palette centered on deep navy, emerald green, warm gold and cool gray.
The design direction calls for a modern sans-serif typeface such as Poppins, Inter or Roboto, supported by a clean grid, generous whitespace and subtle interaction cues.
Navy provides the foundation for trust and professionalism. Green introduces a sense of progress and reliability. Gold is reserved for moments that need emphasis or a sense of value.

Together, the system creates a visual language that can move between property discovery, financial information, legal documentation and service management without feeling like four unrelated products.
extraSections.closing: The UI therefore avoids excessive decoration and instead relies on hierarchy, spacing, typography, cards, status indicators and structured information to create confidence.

extraSections.title: From Screens to a System
paragraphs: Because the platform covers many workflows, designing every screen independently would quickly create inconsistency. Our approach was to think in reusable interface patterns.

Property cards, information cards, status elements, form controls, navigation patterns, dashboard modules, verification indicators, financial summaries and action areas can share the same underlying visual language.

This makes the product easier to extend as new property categories, services and workflows are introduced. The design system is therefore not just a collection of colors and buttons. It is the visual framework that allows a large property ecosystem to feel like one product.

extraSections.title: Responsive Experience
paragraphs: The product was designed as a multi-device digital experience, with particular attention to information-heavy screens.
Property discovery, filters, property details, forms, dashboards, financial tools and service requests all require different responsive behaviors.

The goal is not simply to shrink the desktop interface. Instead, information hierarchy and interaction patterns need to adapt to the available space while preserving the most important actions and property information.

extraSections.title: From UX to UI

items.title: Business and audience
items.body: We started by understanding what Kapital Properties wanted to become, who it needed to serve and how its services connected.

items.title: Product architecture
items.body: We then translated those requirements into product architecture, information hierarchy and user journeys.

items.title: Interface system
items.body: Once the structure was established, we developed the interface system, visual language and responsive experiences around those journeys.

extraSections.closing: This sequence allowed the visual design to follow the product logic rather than becoming a collection of attractive but disconnected screens.

extraSections.title: The Homepage as the Product's Front Door
extraSections.intro: The homepage was designed to communicate the breadth of KPL without overwhelming first-time visitors. The client's proposed structure gave us a clear foundation.
paragraphs: The hero establishes the primary property-search action. Property discovery immediately connects users to inventory. Financing introduces another major part of the ecosystem. Trust-focused content communicates why users should feel comfortable continuing. PNN creates a knowledge layer. Finally, the listing CTA gives property owners a direct entry point into the ecosystem.
extraSections.closing: The result is a homepage that doesn't merely advertise KPL's services. It introduces the different ways users can participate in the platform.

extraSections.title: Development & Product Delivery
paragraphs: Web Karigor's involvement was not limited to producing visual screens. The project was approached as a digital product requiring coordination between business requirements, UX structure, interface design and implementation considerations.

The design work was organized so that complex experiences such as listing, verification, dashboards, property details, financial services and service requests could be understood and translated into development-ready interfaces.

However, the available project material does not document the final engineering stack, hosting architecture, deployment pipeline or individual development technologies. We therefore do not attribute specific technologies or infrastructure to the project here. Likewise, the supplied material does not provide verified production metrics or a documented launch report.

extraSections.title: Designed for an Operational Ecosystem
extraSections.headline: Submit → Review → Process → Update → Complete
paragraphs: A platform like KPL has two sides. There is the experience users see, and there is the operational process behind it.

A property submitted by a seller may need verification. A booking may need administrative processing. A financing request may need documentation. A service request may require a KPL professional. A property-management issue may need follow-up.

The product architecture therefore considers these experiences as connected states rather than isolated actions. That model allows KPL's human expertise to remain part of the digital experience instead of trying to automate every interaction.

groups.title: Product foundation
items: Property discovery — Search, categories, filters, map-based exploration and property information.
Property listing — Structured submission, property details, amenities, pricing, media and supporting documentation.
Trust & verification — Interfaces designed around verified properties, profiles and documentation.
Customer dashboard — A central workspace for listings, favorites, requests, communication and financial activity.
Financing — Eligibility, EMI and loan application experiences.
Communication — Inquiry, messaging and contact workflows.
Property services — Documentation, regulatory, interior and management services.
NRB experience — A service-oriented model for customers managing property from abroad.
Investment ecosystem — Broader Amana-related property and financial service concepts.
PNN — A content and market-insight layer connected to the property experience.
Design system — A consistent visual and interaction foundation across the ecosystem.

extraSections.title: The Result
paragraphs: Kapital Properties was shaped as more than a digital catalogue of properties. The product brings together the different stages and supporting services surrounding property ownership into a single digital ecosystem.
For customers, that means the experience can move from finding a property to understanding it, verifying it, financing it, requesting support, and eventually managing the property.
For Kapital Properties, the platform creates a digital foundation capable of supporting a broader range of property services under one brand.

extraSections.title: A Platform Built Around Trust
paragraphs: The central design challenge was never simply making property search easier. It was creating an environment where users could feel more informed and confident while navigating one of the most complicated categories of personal and financial decision-making.
That is why verification, documentation, financial clarity, service visibility and professional assistance are woven into the product rather than treated as secondary features.
The final direction reflects the client's original philosophy: Property is more than an asset. It is a long-term journey.
extraSections.closing: Web Karigor's role was to turn that philosophy into a structured digital product experience. Strategy · UX · UI · Design System · Product Experience.

probashi-resorts.title: Property Investment Website Design | Probashi Resorts

about.headline: When Intent Meets Uncertainty
about.body: People are ready to invest, but hesitation wins at the last moment. Not due to lack of money, but due to a lack of clarity, structure, and most importantly, trust in the system itself.

more.headline: Listening Before Designing
more.body:
Instead of assuming behavior, I spoke directly with people who showed interest in property investment but never acted on it. Conversations with 8–10 individuals revealed a consistent pattern: interest exists but confidence does not; information is available but not understandable; opportunities exist but are not trusted.

“I want to invest, but I don’t know who to trust.” The challenge was no longer just about usability, it was about designing trust into every step of the experience.

probashi-resorts.clientVoice: Our vision was to build a property-sharing platform that makes property investment simple and accessible. The platform should allow people to explore available projects, understand share ownership, pricing and EMI options, register and make payments, and track their investment progress in one place. We also wanted the experience to communicate the quality of our properties, facilities, design, and development process while creating a trustworthy and transparent digital presence for shareholders.
probashi-resorts.problem:
No Clear Entry Point — Users don’t know how to begin their investment journey. The absence of a structured starting point creates hesitation before any real decision is made.

Trust Is Fragile — Property investment involves high stakes. Without visible proof of authenticity or transparency, users default to caution and avoid taking action.

Invisible Systems — Existing businesses often operate without a clear digital presence or structured communication, making it difficult for users to verify information independently.

Cognitive Overload — Investment details are often scattered, complex, or poorly structured—making it hard for users to understand what they’re committing to.

Result — A gap forms between intent and action, where motivated users drop off before investing.
probashi-resorts.solution:
This was never just about making screens usable. It was about making decisions feel safe. When money is involved, users do not explore freely. They pause, question, and often step back. The design had to reduce that hesitation by aligning with how people actually evaluate risk, trust information, and move toward commitment.

01. Expose the Truth Early — Critical signals like share availability, real project visuals, and pricing clarity are presented upfront instead of being hidden deeper in the flow.

02. Replace Assumptions with Evidence — Testimonials, visible progress updates, and structured payment breakdowns provide users with tangible information they can evaluate.

03. Turn Complexity into Sequence — Investment details are broken into a logical flow from understanding the concept to evaluating the numbers. Pricing, ownership, and payment options are presented in familiar formats.

04. Keep Momentum Visible — The experience continuously communicates what has been done, what remains, and what comes next, so users feel guided rather than lost.

testimonial.quote: Working with Sha Arian on the Probashi Resort website was a great experience. He took the initial requirements and turned them into a clear, structured, and professional digital product. Throughout the project, he understood our business goals, suggested practical improvements, and paid close attention to how users would understand the investment process. The final design feels modern, trustworthy, and easy to navigate, while clearly presenting our projects, share ownership model, payment process, and other important information. We are very satisfied with the final outcome and appreciate the thought and effort he put into bringing our vision to life.
testimonial.name: Théo Cesarini

extraSections.intro: Instead of grouping content by business needs, the architecture is organized around user intent. Each layer introduces information at the moment it becomes relevant, reducing cognitive load and supporting confident decision-making.

groups.title: Decision Trigger

extraSections.title: Trust Isn’t Claimed, it’s Proven
extraSections.intro: In high-risk decisions, users don’t rely on promises. They look for proof. Instead of treating trust as a single feature, the experience is designed to provide continuous, visible evidence that supports user judgment at every step.

groups.title: Make Availability Visible
items: Live share counts are displayed upfront so users can see real demand and remaining opportunity. This removes ambiguity and helps users understand both scarcity and activity within the system.

groups.title: Replace Assumptions with Real Visuals
items: Authentic project images are used instead of generic representations. This allows users to evaluate the property based on actual visuals, reducing reliance on imagination or blind trust.

groups.title: Let Users Validate Through Others
items: Testimonials are presented as supporting signals from existing participants. They provide context and reassurance by showing that others have already engaged with the system.

groups.title: Break Down Financial Commitment Clearly
items: Payment structures are shown in detail during key decision moments. Users can see exactly what they are paying, how it is structured, and what to expect over time.

groups.title: Show Progress Beyond the Purchase
items: Construction updates are accessible after investment, allowing users to track real-world progress. This extends trust beyond the initial decision and keeps users informed over time.

groups.title: Balance Transparency with Control
items: Legal and sensitive documents are made available to verified users when relevant. This ensures transparency without exposing critical information unnecessarily.

extraSections.title: Trust Moves Through People
extraSections.intro: In high-risk decisions, people rarely trust systems alone. They trust people who have already taken the step. Instead of relying only on platform credibility, the experience extends trust through human connections, allowing users to validate decisions through their own network.

groups.title: Familiar Entry Points
items: Users can invite friends and family into the system, turning a complex investment decision into a shared conversation. This lowers the psychological barrier by replacing unknown systems with known relations.

groups.title: Transparent Referral Tracking
items: A dedicated dashboard allows users to track referrals, activity, and outcomes in real time. This creates clarity around participation and removes ambiguity from the process.

groups.title: Visible Incentive Structure
items: Earnings and rewards are clearly presented, helping users understand the value of participation beyond investment. This aligns motivation with action without relying on hidden mechanics.

groups.title: Trust That Scales Organically
items: Each new participant enters through an existing connection, reinforcing credibility at every step. The system grows not just through acquisition, but through layered trust built between people.

extraSections.title: Design That Carries Meaning
extraSections.headline: Visual design here is not used to impress. It is used to guide judgment.
paragraphs: Every choice, from color to layout, is aligned with how users interpret risk, value, and credibility in a financial context.

Manrope (Font Family) — Reading should never feel like work, especially when money is involved. A clean, modern type system ensures clear hierarchy and fast scanning. Information is structured so users can quickly identify what matters without reading everything line by line, reducing cognitive load during decision-making.

Spacing, grouping, and visual hierarchy work together to surface important information at the right moment. This helps users process complex details in smaller, manageable chunks instead of facing everything at once.
extraSections.closing: Desktop View: 1920px · Container: 1520px

groups.title: First Signal of Trust
items: The entry point answers two questions instantly: what this is and why it matters. A strong headline, contextual subtext, and dynamic project visuals reduce initial confusion and establish credibility. Instead of pushing action too early, this section helps users orient themselves, which is essential for building early-stage confidence.

groups.title: Clarity Before Commitment
items: Investment is explained through a structured flow supported by real numbers. Pricing, available shares, and clear calls to action are placed alongside the ownership model so users can connect the concept with actual commitment.

groups.title: From Vision to Reality
items: The hero introduces the project visually and geographically, while the architecture section explains its intent, purpose, and overall concept. Together, they help users move beyond surface-level attraction and understand what they are considering.

groups.title: Details That Hold Up Under Scrutiny
items: Detailed specifications provide clarity on what the project includes, while the prospectus offers deeper documentation for those who want full transparency. Amenities highlight added value from a lifestyle and utility perspective.

groups.title: Opportunities, Made Scannable
items: Available projects are presented as structured, comparable cards so users can explore without friction. Each card balances key information with clear actions like viewing details or downloading the prospectus.

extraSections.title: From Idea to Built Reality
paragraphs: These moments capture how ideas move beyond sketches and discussions into real, tangible outcomes. From early thinking to collaboration with engineers and domain experts, every step is aligned toward one goal: delivering spaces that are not only designed well, but built with intention and quality.

Probashi Resort approaches development as a continuous translation process, where vision is refined, validated, and executed with precision. For shareholders, this means their investment is not just a concept on paper, but a real asset shaped through expertise, structure, and accountability.
extraSections.closing: The result is not just architecture — it’s confidence made visible through execution.

extraSections.title: Designing for Real Impact
extraSections.intro: Impact is not always captured in numbers. It shows up in behavior. When users hesitate less, understand faster, and move forward with confidence, design is doing its job. This work focused on reshaping those moments where people usually pause, doubt, or drop off.

groups.title: Less Friction, More Forward Movement
items: A structured flow reduces unnecessary thinking at each step. By guiding users clearly from discovery to action, the experience removes decision bottlenecks that typically slow users down.

groups.title: Visibility That Replaces Doubt
items: Uncertainty often comes from what users cannot see. By surfacing key information such as progress, pricing, and availability, the system allows users to evaluate decisions without relying on assumptions.

groups.title: Confidence Built Over Time
items: Trust is not created in a single interaction. Layered signals across the journey help users gradually feel more certain about their decisions instead of forcing early commitment.

groups.title: Growth Through Participation
items: Users are not just end points in the system. With referral-driven interactions, they become part of how the platform expands, turning trust into a shared experience rather than an isolated one.
